name: London Ambulance Service
description: The London Ambulance Service dispatches ambulances in emergencies. The key goal is to allocate an available ambulance for every call that can reach the scene within 11 minutes. The entire dispatch process must not exceed a set maximum time limit. The Computer Aided Despatch system analyzes incident forms and assigns vehicles. The exact location of moving ambulances must be tracked, requiring ambulance staff to follow standard routes and communicate departure and destination information so that radio operators and the CAD can accurately record the corresponding data.
highLevelGoals: Ambulance Staff aim to reach emergency scenes within the critical 11-minute target to provide immediate medical assistance.
Ambulance Staff need to accurately communicate their departure, destination, and current location to ensure the CAD system and Radio Operators have real-time information.
Ambulance Staff must follow standard routes and communication protocols to facilitate efficient dispatch and tracking.
Radio Operators aim to precisely record all departure, destination, and location updates from Ambulance Staff to maintain an accurate overview of available resources.
Radio Operators seek to ensure that all recorded ambulance data is promptly and accurately transmitted to the Computer Aided Despatch (CAD) system.
The Dispatcher's primary goal is to assign an available ambulance to every emergency call, ensuring it can reach the scene within 11 minutes.
The Dispatcher aims to complete the entire dispatch process within a set maximum time limit to minimize response delays.
The Dispatcher needs the CAD system to accurately analyze incident forms to make informed decisions when assigning vehicles.
The Dispatcher requires accurate and up-to-date tracking of moving ambulances to make optimal dispatch decisions.
lowLevelGoals: Ambulance Staff will transmit their current GPS coordinates to the system.
Ambulance Staff will set their status to 'en route' to the emergency scene.
Ambulance Staff will update their status to 'on scene' once they have arrived at the emergency location.
Ambulance Staff will send a timestamp indicating their departure from the ambulance base.
Ambulance Staff will input and send the exact destination address for the emergency incident.
Ambulance Staff's vehicle will automatically send its current GPS coordinates at regular intervals.
Ambulance Staff will choose a standard, pre-approved route for the assigned emergency.
Ambulance Staff will establish communication using the specified radio frequency or digital channel.
Ambulance Staff will acknowledge and confirm that they have received and understood dispatch instructions.
Radio Operators will input the exact time an ambulance departs from its base into the system.
Radio Operators will enter the destination address provided by Ambulance Staff for an incident.
Radio Operators will change an ambulance's status (e.g., 'en route', 'on scene', 'available') in the system based on verbal or digital updates.
Radio Operators will send the logged ambulance departure time to the Computer Aided Despatch (CAD) system.
Radio Operators will send the logged ambulance destination to the Computer Aided Despatch (CAD) system.
Radio Operators will ensure that all changes in ambulance status are immediately reflected in the CAD system.
The Dispatcher will view a graphical representation of all available ambulances on the CAD system's map.
The Dispatcher will click or otherwise select a specific available ambulance to assign to an emergency call.
The Dispatcher will finalize the assignment of the selected ambulance to the emergency incident.
The Dispatcher will be notified by the CAD system when a new emergency incident is reported.
The Dispatcher will open the digital form containing all relevant information about the emergency incident.
The Dispatcher will trigger the process to send dispatch instructions to the chosen ambulance.
The Dispatcher will see the classification and urgency of the emergency from the incident form.
The Dispatcher will review information regarding the patient's medical state as provided in the incident form.
The Dispatcher will identify any specific equipment or personnel requirements for the ambulance based on the incident details.
The CAD system will show the current positions of all ambulances that are currently deployed or in transit.
The CAD system will visually indicate the current operational status of each ambulance.
The CAD system will compute and display the projected arrival time for ambulances to incident locations.
